chunks: And Ḥarīz narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man to whom domestic pigeons were gifted and brought while he was in the Ḥaram and not in iḥrām. He said: “If he takes any of it, then he should give charity in its place, approximately equivalent to its price.”

key_terms.الْحَرَمِ: the sacred sanctuary in which special legal restrictions apply
key_terms.حَمَامٌ أَهْلِيٌّ: domestic pigeons, as opposed to wild game
key_terms.فَلْيَتَصَدَّقْ: let him give charity as required compensation
key_terms.مُحِلٌّ: a person not in the state of iḥrām

ai.seo_question: What must someone do if domestic pigeons are gifted to him in the Ḥaram and he takes from them?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning domestic pigeons brought as a gift to a person in the Ḥaram while he is not in iḥrām. If he makes use of them, he must give charity roughly equal to their value as compensation.
